items.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
items.raw_content: Existing vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception. In this report, we present WeVisOne-VL (WeChat Vision All-in-One), a powerful VLM that unifies object-level and pixel-level perception through structured next-token prediction. It supports multiple visual tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting, enabling localization at any user-specific granularity, from points and boxes to masks and alpha mattes. Architecturally, we integrate a lightweight pixel decoder into the VLM via a special <OBJ> token to generate instance-level pixel outputs. We train the model with a three-stage curriculum SFT followed by mixed-task RL. Across over 30 benchmarks, WeVisOne-VL demonstrates leading performance on both object-level and pixel-level tasks, while maintaining robust rejection for object-absent queries.
items.title_zh: WeVisOne-VL：从物体到像素的统一视觉感知
items.summary: WeVisOne-VL is a vision-language model that handles both object-level and pixel-level perception by predicting structured tokens, covering segmentation, matting, OCR, counting, referring localization and detection.

items.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
items.raw_content: Cinematic video generation requires both temporal inference from limited inputs (i.e., sparse rather than frame-by-frame guidance) and factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer useful priors for both capabilities, but their representations are not automatically actionable for video generation: a Video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) may bypass them through native conditioning pathways, and using them does not ensure either factor-aware control or generation-compatible temporal prediction. We propose Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL), which establishes effective MLLM latent use as a shared prerequisite and then targets the two capabilities with complementary learning signals. First, latent-only generator grounding trains the DiT with a frozen MLLM and connector, strengthening the DiT's use of MLLM latents for generation.
items.title_zh: 让多模态大模型潜变量真正起作用
items.summary: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning makes MLLM latents actionable for cinematic video generation, adding latent-only grounding plus complementary signals for factor-aware control of character, scene, action and camera.

items.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
items.raw_content: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editin
items.title_zh: 把图像编辑成可复用图层
items.summary: LayerEditor couples instruction-guided image editing with generation of reusable RGBA layers, representing the edited canvas and ordered layers in one token sequence and distilling the base model's editing prior to preserve quality.

items.title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
items.raw_content: Despite substantial progress in Deep Search agents, their ability to conduct end-to-end research in real-world open Web environments remains insufficiently evaluated. Unlike static retrieval settings, information on the real-world Web is distributed across diverse sources, modalities, and heterogeneous formats, often involving complex interaction mechanisms that require agents to autonomously search for, access, and integrate relevant evidence during execution. To address this gap, we introduce the OpenDS task, designed to evaluate agents' ability to perform multi-step deep search in the live, open Web. This task requires agents to autonomously explore the real Web, discover and connect relevant evidence from multiple independent sources through Web search, browser interaction, and evidence processing, and ultimately determine a unique factual answer. Building on this task formulation, w
items.title_zh: 真实网络环境中的深度搜索
items.summary: The paper introduces OpenDS, a task for evaluating deep-search agents on the live open web, where agents must search, browse and integrate evidence from multiple independent sources to find a unique factual answer.

items.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
items.raw_content: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future
items.title_zh: 为世界动作模型自蒸馏未来视频表征
items.summary: FRED uses self-distillation with temporal context to teach world action models to produce future video representations from noise in one denoising step, improving the features that action decoders rely on.

items.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
items.raw_content: As model parameters scale up, sparsely activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches have become essential for model scaling. However, mainstream models currently adopt hierarchical architectures, where experts in different layers, although topologically independent, exhibit substantial similarity and redundancy in their stored content. Compared to the hierarchically arranged Local Expert in existing mainstream models, we hypothesize that inter-layer shared Meta Expert hold greater potential. To this end, we conduct a multi-dimensional empirical comparison between Local and Meta Experts, and find that models incorporating Meta Experts exhibit lower parameter redundancy, together with lower cross-entropy loss and higher downstream task accuracy. With the activated quantity and the expert granularity held fixed, our model matches the performance of Vanilla MoE using only 70--80\% of the ex
items.title_zh: Meta Expert：跨层专家共享的高效 MoE
items.summary: Meta Expert shares experts across layers in sparse MoE models; the authors report lower parameter redundancy and matching vanilla MoE performance using only 70-80% of the experts.

items.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
items.raw_content: Fine-grained visual understanding requires distinguishing subtle differences in local attributes and spatial relations, yet remains challenging for existing vision-language models. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) offer a new opportunity through generation pathways that preserve rich visual information complementary to understanding. However, existing generation-assisted understanding methods mainly rely on generative supervision or explicit generation and have not systematically explored direct use of native generation-side representations. To address this gap, we systematically analyze what generation-side representations offer for fine-grained understanding, finding that they are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes, capture task-relevant changes missed by understanding-side representations, and depend on correct spatial organization for this advantage. Guided by these find
items.title_zh: 生成知道什么：释放统一多模态模型的细粒度理解
items.summary: The paper analyzes native generation-side representations in unified multimodal models, finding they are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic change and can improve fine-grained visual understanding.

items.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
items.raw_content: Code-based video generation offers fine-grained control, targeted editing, and component reuse compared with direct video generation. This approach requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to translate visual and temporal requirements into executable programs that produce complete videos. However, existing code-based benchmarks primarily target specialized tasks, leaving complete video creation across diverse creative categories and input modalities insufficiently evaluated. We introduce Code2Video-Compass, a general-purpose benchmark for code-based video generation across text-to-video (T2V), image-to-video (I2V), and video-to-video (V2V) settings. Code2Video-Compass comprises 2,104 tasks spanning 10 categories, 24 subtypes, and three complexity dimensions covering construction, dynamic animation, and state dependency. It combines tasks curated from textual instructions and vis
items.title_zh: Code2Video-Compass：代码生成视频综合评测
items.summary: Code2Video-Compass is a benchmark of 2,104 tasks across 10 categories for code-based video generation in text-to-video, image-to-video and video-to-video settings, covering construction, animation and state dependency.

items.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
items.raw_content: LLM memory is widely used in long-term conversation understanding. Agentic memory systems often use mutation, structural organization, learned retrieval strategies, or other complex operations. Is this complexity always necessary? We study Raw-RAG, a naive RAG baseline using dense retrieval and reranking over raw history to supply evidence to a reader LLM. Across LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MEME, and MemoryAgentBench, Raw-RAG ranks first among the compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings, outperforming the strongest compared agentic memory system by 0.13-5.53 points. We investigate why raw-history retrieval remains competitive. Evidence analysis shows that its higher coverage of necessary evidence can offset lower utilization. Useful evidence includes both answer values and the relations and dependency paths needed to derive them. Even complete access to transformed memo
items.title_zh: 真的需要复杂智能体记忆吗？朴素 RAG 比想象中更强
items.summary: A simple Raw-RAG baseline that retrieves and reranks raw conversation history with dense methods ranks first in six of seven benchmark-model settings, beating the best agentic memory system by 0.13-5.53 points.

items.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks
items.raw_content: Selecting intermediate features from a frozen diffusion model for discriminative tasks is non-trivial because the useful signal is distributed across the denoising trajectory, network depth, and channels. In practice, this requires choosing a timestep, a block, and a channel subset. Existing methods either fix these choices by hand or optimize only a few extraction hyperparameters, most often the timestep, then reuse the same rule across inputs and budgets. We introduce Policy-Mask, a budget-conditioned policy trained on the downstream objective that jointly selects all three under a prescribed channel budget. Without normalization, the channel-score contribution grows with the number of selected channels and dominates the timestep and block updates. We normalize it by subset cardinality, keeping the three policy heads on comparable scales and stabilizing joint training. At matched budge
items.title_zh: Policy-Mask：按预算适配扩散特征
items.summary: Policy-Mask trains a budget-conditioned policy to jointly choose timestep, block and channel subset from a frozen diffusion model for discriminative tasks, normalizing channel scores by subset size to stabilize training.

items.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
items.raw_content: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. The Director is supported by three specialized agents: an Interpreter that extracts scene-grounded cinematographic intent, a Scout that selects initial viewpoints, and a Critic that evaluates rendered results and provides visual feedback for iterative plan refinement. We also introduce CinemaBench, comprising 150 Blender scenes from self-created and lic
items.title_zh: FilmFlow：3D 虚拟影视摄影智能体系统
items.summary: FilmFlow turns natural-language instructions or reference videos into executable camera trajectories in 3D environments using Director, Interpreter, Scout and Critic agents; it also introduces CinemaBench with 150 Blender scenes.

items.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
items.raw_content: Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance. We introduce Heartbeat Thinking, which handles updated input through new Thinker invocations while allowing ongoing invocations and dispatched tools to finish. Periodic invocations read the latest partial transcript and a shared record of completed reasoning and tool results. These results help resolve missing arguments and initiate dependent calls, allowing preparation to progress across speech updates. Across SpeechFCEval, FDBench v3, and AudioCRAG, Heartbeat improves aggregate speculative tool coverage or
items.title_zh: 心跳思考：实时语音智能体边听边推理与调用工具
items.summary: Heartbeat Thinking lets realtime voice agents start speculative reasoning and tool calls on partial transcripts while earlier invocations finish, improving speculative tool coverage on SpeechFCEval, FDBench v3 and AudioCRAG.
